subject: Hosted API — residency, retention & erasure workflow Q&A
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@orchidhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: support@orchidhealth.com
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API — questions on residency, retention, erasure

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for taking this. We're preparing a short security questionnaire to assess whether Orchid Health can use Redwood's hosted API for patient-facing features. A few clarifying questions around data residency, retention, and deletion before we loop in procurement/legal: 

1) Where is customer request/response data stored by default (region)? Can we guarantee entry/exit in a specific geography?
2) What are the default retention windows for: a) raw request/response payloads, b) logs/audit trails, c) backups/snapshots, d) model cache (prefix/KV cache)?
3) If we request account-level deletion, what is the SLA for: a) removing data from live systems, b) removing data from backups and snapshots, c) confirmation evidence?
4) Can logging of full request payloads be disabled for our account (we may want only aggregated telemetry retained)?
5) Are request/response bodies accessible to humans at Redwood for debugging? How is access controlled/audited?
6) For hosted customers, do you offer customer-managed keys (BYOK) or HSM options?
7) Any compliance constraints we should be aware of for PHI (if we elect to sign a BAA)?

I've attached Orchid's questionnaire (first tab has the items we care about). If you could provide short, copy-ready answers that we can include in our internal review that would be ideal.

Appreciate it —
Elena
Orchid Health — Security & Risk

Attachment: Orchid_Security_Form_v3.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API — questions on residency, retention, erasure

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise, copy-ready answers you can drop into your questionnaire; I added a brief note on regional options and operational SLAs at the end. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call to walk through if helpful.

1) Default region: For standard Hosted API accounts we persist request/response data and associated logs in the region selected at account creation; for new Orchid accounts the default is us-west-2 (Oregon). We can provision an EU region for accounts that need Europe-only residency (subject to contractual agreement).

2) Default retention windows (Hosted API):
  - Raw request/response payloads (complete request/response bodies): retained for up to 30 days for debugging and quality monitoring; customers can request shorter retention in the account settings or via support.
  - Logs & audit trails (API metadata, request timestamps, routing, and operator access logs): retained for 365 days by default. Audit logs include IAM events and human access records.
  - Backups & snapshots: full-system backups and warm snapshots are kept for up to 90 days; snapshots are used for disaster recovery and are purged on a rolling basis.
  - Model prefix/KV cache: transient by design; entries are ephemeral (typical TTL ~24 hours) and can be disabled for a tenant by request. Cached entries are not treated as long-term persistent storage.

3) Account-level deletion SLA and procedure (Hosted API):
  a) Live systems: when Orchid requests account deletion or data purge, we remove customer data from live stores within 7 business days and confirm via support ticket.
  b) Backups/snapshots: purging from backups is a longer window — snapshots are scheduled for deletion and may take up to 90 days to be fully irrecoverable depending on snapshot lifecycle and replication windows.
  c) Evidence: we provide a deletion statement (signed PDF) that includes the deletion timestamp, scope, and the support ticket reference once the live purge completes. Final confirmation after backup purge is provided when the snapshot retention window expires (we log the action and provide the timestamp).

Notes: Legal holds or active investigations can suspend the backup purge timeline; in those cases we coordinate with your legal team and provide status updates.

4) Logging of full request payloads: We provide a per-account setting to disable full payload logging (store-only-aggregates). When disabled, the system will still keep minimal metadata required for billing and rate-limiting but will not persist raw inputs/outputs. Note: disabling payload logging reduces our ability to debug specific user issues; we typically recommend a short retention window and access controls as a compromise.

5) Human access: Full request/response payloads in live systems are strictly restricted. Access requires a documented, role-based access request, approval by security, and is logged in the audit trail. All such accesses are subject to quarterly review. Operator access to customer payloads is rare and tied to explicit, tracked debugging sessions.

6) Customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM): For Hosted API we default to provider-managed encryption keys (AES-256 at rest, with region-bound KMS). Customer-managed KMS (BYOK) is available for Enterprise accounts under contract (we can require a dedicated key per-account in supported regions). For full HSM-backed key control we typically recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.

7) PHI/BAA: We can sign a BAA with enterprise customers and have operational controls designed to support reasonable HIPAA requirements (access controls, audit trails, encryption in transit and at rest, limited payload retention, logging controls). Any PHI usage should be scoped in the DPA/BAA during contracting.

Operational/other items:
- If Orchid requires EU-only data residency, we will provision account resources in an EU region and restrict cross-region backups as part of the contractual settings.
- For urgent deletions (e.g. legal erasure notices), we offer an expedited delete process (SLA: 48–72 hours for live stores) as an add-on for Enterprise customers — we'll need an authorized contact and PO.
- We maintain SOC 2 Type II and can surface a copy of our report under NDA.

Attachments referenced: redwood-dataflow-diagram.png (high-level flow showing where data persists and where caching occurs).

Next steps: If this looks good, I can attach a DPA draft and loop in our Legal to finalize PHI/BAA language.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Aditya — adding a short legal-ready paragraph we should send with the DPA. Please replace any informal phrasing if you paste this into the questionnaire: 

"Redwood Inference processes Customer Data in the region selected at account provision. For Hosted API customers, Customer Data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256). Default retention settings are 30 days for request/response bodies and 365 days for operational logs unless otherwise specified in a signed Data Processing Addendum. Account-level erasure requests will be executed in accordance with the contract and applicable law; removal from live stores is completed within seven business days, with removal from backups occurring according to snapshot lifecycle (up to 90 days). Redwood will provide a deletion attestation upon completion of each stage. Exceptions for legal hold or compliance investigations can extend retention beyond these windows."

I attached a DPA draft (Redwood_DPA_Draft.pdf) that includes the PHI/BAA section we discussed previously. If Orchid confirms PHI scope we'll route the BAA addendum.

-Neha
VP Legal — Redwood Inference
